tagline: Up through the pines, then down the switchbacks into Jerome.
intro: On the Prescott Valley side, SR 89A starts up out of Yaeger Canyon at the base of the Black Hills, ponderosa pine hugging the road among pockets of basalt. It winds through narrow canyons between Mingus and Woodchute mountains. Over the top the Mogollon Rim and the Verde Valley open out ahead, and a steep drop brings it to Jerome.
The ore drew people long before the road. Spanish explorers located claims here in 1582 and 1598 and never worked them, and the deposits waited until Army troops came across them again in 1875.

moments.title: Mingus Mountain
moments.text: Forest roads climb from the highway to the top, where the Mingus Lookout fire tower complex is on the National Register, and the mountain is a flying site for hang gliders and paragliders.

moments.title: Jerome
moments.text: In the 1930s the ground sank away under dozens of Jerome's buildings, the jail among them, and after the mines closed in 1953 a town that had held more than 10,000 fell below 100.

practical: ADOT's corridor plan describes the mountain road as two lanes with no standard shoulder, many switchbacks and long stretches of guardrail.
